# Game Table

> Game Table is a platform for multiplayer board and card games at a real table: a touchscreen board lying flat, each player's phone as their private deck, AI players, and remote players who join through an invite. A game is a folder with a manifest, pure deterministic rules in TypeScript, and optional plain-JavaScript UI modules for the board and the phones; the platform does everything else (lobby, seats, players joining, leaving and being exchanged, AI scheduling, pauses, logs, replay, statistics, remote play).

**Installing it on one computer to play** (Windows 11, macOS or Linux, phones on the same WiFi): download the package for the system from https://github.com/klaushofrichter/games-service/releases/tag/local-table and follow its install guide: https://games.skylar.technology/docs/install/windows.md, https://games.skylar.technology/docs/install/macos.md or https://games.skylar.technology/docs/install/linux.md. Each package brings its own Node.js, needs no Docker and no service, and asks for the private game repositories the user can read; each guide has a section for an AI agent doing the installation.

**Installing it locally with Docker** (a table on one machine, phones on the same network): follow the runbook https://games.skylar.technology/docs/local-docker.md step by step. Docker is all it needs: no cloud service or console, no DNS entry, no HTTPS, nothing from games.skylar.technology. Games from other repositories, private ones included, are added by cloning them (runbook Part B); no token or console is involved.

Read the developer guide before writing or changing a game. It is the contract between games and the platform, written for language models as much as for people. The platform's code is the final word: `packages/sdk/src/index.ts` (the rules API) and `packages/protocol/src/index.ts` (the manifest schema and lobby types) in the public repository https://github.com/klaushofrichter/games-service. For a complete game repository of its own to copy (five games, tests against the platform, CI), see the public example https://github.com/klaushofrichter/extra-games.

Key rules for every game: rules are pure and deterministic (randomness only from `ctx.random()`, time only from `ctx.now()`, never mutate the given state); a seat's view never contains another seat's secrets; a running game always keeps all its players, and the platform owns joining, leaving, away phones and exchanging players (a game only reacts in `onSeatChanged`); AI players read only their seat's view; a game's version changes with every change in its folder.

## Developer guide

- [Writing a game for Game Table](https://games.skylar.technology/docs/game-development.md): the full contract, with a checklist (the same file in the repository: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/klaushofrichter/games-service/main/docs/developers/game-development.md)
- [Everything in one file](https://games.skylar.technology/llms-full.txt): this index followed by the whole guide and the Docker runbook

## API reference (source)

- [Rules SDK](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/klaushofrichter/games-service/main/packages/sdk/src/index.ts): `defineGame`, `GameDefinition` with every hook, `GameContext`, `SeatInfo`, `count`, `list`, `mostAward`, `leastAward`
- [Cards helpers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/klaushofrichter/games-service/main/packages/sdk/src/cards.ts): deck, seeded shuffle, poker hand evaluation
- [Manifest schema and lobby types](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/klaushofrichter/games-service/main/packages/protocol/src/index.ts): `manifestSchema`, `GameSummary`, `GameAward`, `PlayerInfo`, `LobbyState`
- [Board kit for UI modules](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/klaushofrichter/games-service/main/apps/table-host/public/shared/board-kit.js): seat plates, player colours, rotation, countdowns, sounds, styles
- [Sling](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/klaushofrichter/games-service/main/apps/table-host/public/shared/sling.js): a card (or die, token) pushed off the top of a phone comes onto the board at the player's seat and flies to its place; drawn cards fly back (developer guide, section 10)
- [Game log format](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/klaushofrichter/games-service/main/apps/table-host/src/log-format.md): records, move lists, replay

## Example games

- [Coin Flip](https://github.com/klaushofrichter/games-service/tree/main/games/coin-flip): the smallest complete game (simultaneous guesses, timers, statistics, players joining mid-game, board and phone UIs, rules for players)
- [Pachisi](https://github.com/klaushofrichter/games-service/tree/main/games/pachisi): turns, dice, captures, moves made by touching the board, `describe` for the Game Viewer
- [Hold'em](https://github.com/klaushofrichter/games-service/tree/main/games/holdem): private cards, AI styles, awards, a skippable wait, sounds
- [Roulette](https://github.com/klaushofrichter/games-service/tree/main/games/roulette): simultaneous betting, AI styles
- [Example game repository](https://github.com/klaushofrichter/extra-games): Chess, Liar's Dice, Backgammon, Mexican Train and Last Card (a full example of the sling) in a repository of their own (public), tested against games-service with CI; the layout to copy for a new game repository

## Running it

- Packages for one computer, for players: [Windows](https://games.skylar.technology/docs/install/windows.md), [macOS](https://games.skylar.technology/docs/install/macos.md), [Linux](https://games.skylar.technology/docs/install/linux.md): install guides for the packages on https://github.com/klaushofrichter/games-service/releases/tag/local-table (installer, `.pkg`, `.tar.gz`; Node.js included, no Docker, no service)
- [Run Game Table locally with Docker](https://games.skylar.technology/docs/local-docker.md): the runbook for a local installation, written for agents: the Table Host with the built-in games on one machine, phones on the LAN, no cloud service, DNS or HTTPS; games from other repositories, private ones by cloning; optionally a local cloud service (the same file in the repository: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/klaushofrichter/games-service/main/docs/runbooks/local-docker.md)

- **Without Docker:** `scripts/local-table.sh` (macOS or Linux, Node 26) runs a table from the latest `main` or any `--branch`, with `--extra ../other-repo` for games not released yet (developer guide, section 14).
- **The board on another screen:** an iPad, a TV or a second computer on the same network can show the board while the table runs elsewhere: board settings › *Board on another screen…* gives a QR code and link that move the board there and remember that screen. Same network only; the link carries the table key, so only for your own screens (README, "The board on another screen").

## Testing

- [Rules test harness](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/klaushofrichter/games-service/main/tests/harness.ts): run a game on the real runtime with virtual time, check exact replay
- [Host test helpers](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/klaushofrichter/games-service/main/tests/helpers.ts): a real Table Host with fake phones

## Optional

- [Platform README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/klaushofrichter/games-service/main/README.md): running a table, the board control API, extra-game repositories, remote play, logs
- [Relays for remote play](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/klaushofrichter/games-service/main/docs/runbooks/remote-play-relays.md): when a remote player on a phone's hotspot or cellular data can't connect, a TURN relay (Cloudflare's, optional) for a game service: set up, check, troubleshoot
- [Decision log](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/klaushofrichter/games-service/main/docs/decisions.md): why the platform behaves as it does
